decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins chapter 17 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 16 ends at verse 35, and the account of the censers and the plague (17:1-15 here) follows as the start of chapter 17. Many Bibles number these verses 16:36-50, and so number the rest of this chapter (17:16-28 here) 17:1-13. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

records.literal_gloss: Say to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, and let him lift up the censers from between the burning, and the fire scatter far away, for they are holy.

en.R: "Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, to pick up the censers from where the fire burned. He must scatter the coals far away, because the censers are holy.

sw.B: "Mwambie Eleazari mwana wa Haruni kuhani aviondoe vyetezo kutoka kwenye mabaki yaliyoungua, na kuyatawanya makaa mbali, kwa sababu vyetezo hivyo ni vitakatifu.

decisions.choice: censers: fire pans for carrying burning coals
decisions.reason: A censer was a shallow pan in which burning coals were carried and incense laid on them (Leviticus 10:1; 16:12). These are the censers of the 250 men who offered incense and were burned up by fire from the LORD (16:17-18, 35).

decisions.choice: the burning: the place where the men were burned, and what was left there
decisions.reason: The word means a burning or the remains of a fire (Leviticus 10:6). Eleazar is to lift the censers out from among the charred remains of the men and their fire.

decisions.choice: scatter the fire, for they are holy: the coals are thrown away, the censers kept
decisions.reason: The fire in the censers was not fire the LORD had asked for, so it is scattered far off and not used (compare Leviticus 10:1). The censers themselves had been brought before the LORD and so had become holy (verse 3). They could not go back to common use, even though the men who carried them had sinned.

decisions.choice: they are holy: the censers, not the men
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and comes just after "the fire". Verse 3 explains that it is the censers that became holy, because they were presented before the LORD. Verse 3 also goes straight on with "the censers of these sinners", so the sentence runs across the two verses.

decisions.choice: that he is to lift up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the command to Eleazar to the instruction to tell him. Literal keeps it as reported speech; Balanced and Readable say "tell Eleazar to".

decisions.choice: the coals
decisions.reason: The "fire" in a censer was its burning coals, so Balanced and Readable name them.

records.literal_gloss: the censers of the sinners the these against their lives, and make them hammered-out sheets, plating for the altar; for they brought them near before Yahweh, and they became holy; and let them be for a sign to [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: the censers of these who sinned against their own lives. And make them into hammered sheets, a plating for the altar, for they presented them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they became holy; and let them be a sign to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel."

en.R: These men sinned, and it cost them their lives. Have their censers hammered into thin sheets of metal to cover the altar. The censers were offered to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, so they belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They will be a warning sign for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}."

es.R: Estos hombres pecaron, y eso les costó la vida. {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} que martillen sus incensarios hasta convertirlos en láminas delgadas de metal para cubrir el altar. sw.L: vyetezo vya hawa waliotenda dhambi juu ya nafsi zao wenyewe. Na mvifanye mabamba yaliyofuliwa, kifuniko cha madhabahu, kwa maana walivileta mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, navyo vikawa vitakatifu; na viwe ishara kwa wana wa Israeli."
sw.B: Watu hawa walitenda dhambi iliyowagharimu maisha yao. Mvifue vyetezo vyao kuwa mabamba membamba ya kufunika madhabahu. Vililetwa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa hiyo vimekuwa vitakatifu. Viwe ishara kwa Waisraeli."
sw.R: Watu hawa walitenda dhambi, nayo ikawagharimu maisha yao. Mvifue vyetezo vyao viwe mabamba membamba ya chuma ya kufunika madhabahu. Vyetezo hivyo vilitolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa hiyo ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Vitakuwa ishara ya onyo kwa Waisraeli."

decisions.choice: against their own lives: at the cost of their lives
decisions.reason: "In their lives" means that their sin cost them their lives. They were burned up when they offered incense without being priests (16:35). The same phrase is used of a word spoken at the cost of one's life (1 Kings 2:23).

decisions.choice: hammered sheets as plating for the altar: a bronze covering for the altar of burnt offering
decisions.reason: The censers were bronze (verse 4). They were beaten flat into thin sheets and laid over the bronze altar that stood in front of the tent (Exodus 27:1-2; 38:1-2), so that everyone who came to sacrifice would see them.

decisions.choice: they presented them before the LORD, and they became holy
decisions.reason: Anything offered to the LORD belonged to him from then on and could not be used for common things (Leviticus 27:28). The men's sin did not undo this; it is why the censers are kept at the altar.

decisions.choice: a sign: a visible reminder and warning
decisions.reason: A sign is something seen that points to a truth. Verse 5 says what this one is to remind Israel of: only Aaron's descendants may burn incense before the LORD. The budding staff becomes a second sign later in the chapter (verse 25).

decisions.choice: the censers of these who sinned against their own lives.
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence goes straight on from verse 2: "for they are holy, the censers of these sinners". Literal keeps that link with a colon at the end of verse 2. Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence about the men.

decisions.choice: so they belong to him
decisions.reason: Readable says what "became holy" means here: they were now the LORD's.

decisions.choice: plural command "{{plural_you:háganlos|hacedlos}}", "{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}}"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "make" is plural: the order goes to those who will do the work, not to Moses alone. Spanish keeps the plural, as the brief sets for the number of "you".

decisions.choice: plural "faites-en", "Faites marteler"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "make" is plural, addressed to those who will do the work; French follows the Hebrew number.

decisions.choice: plural "mvifanye", "Mvifue"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb "make" is plural, addressed to those who will do the work; Swahili follows the Hebrew number.

en.L: And Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers which those who were burned had presented, and they hammered them out [as] a plating for the altar,
en.B: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that had been presented by the men who were burned, and they were hammered out to cover the altar,
en.R: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men who were burned up had offered. The censers were hammered flat to cover the altar.

fr.B: Le prêtre Éléazar prit donc les encensoirs de bronze qu’avaient présentés les hommes qui avaient été brûlés, et on les martela pour recouvrir l’autel,

sw.L: Naye Eleazari kuhani akavichukua vyetezo vya shaba vilivyoletwa na wale walioteketezwa, nao wakavifua [kuwa] kifuniko cha madhabahu,
sw.B: Basi Eleazari kuhani akavichukua vyetezo vya shaba vilivyoletwa na watu walioteketezwa, navyo vikafuliwa ili kufunika madhabahu,

decisions.choice: those who were burned: the 250 men consumed by fire from the LORD
decisions.reason: The word looks back to 16:35, where fire came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who offered the incense.

decisions.choice: they hammered them out: the work was done by others
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, though Eleazar alone is named. It means the censers were hammered out under his charge, by those who did such work.

decisions.choice: were hammered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive for the unnamed "they" who did the work.

source.text: זִכָּר֞וֹן לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְ֠מַעַן אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יִקְרַ֜ב אִ֣ישׁ זָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹ֣א מִזֶּ֤רַע אַהֲרֹן֙ ה֔וּא לְהַקְטִ֥יר קְטֹ֖רֶת לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה כְקֹ֨רַח֙ וְכַ֣עֲדָת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: a reminder for [the] sons of Israel, so that not draw near a man strange who not from [the] offspring of Aaron he to burn incense before Yahweh, and not be like Korah and like his congregation, as spoke Yahweh by [the] hand of Moses to him.

en.L: a reminder to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, so that no outsider who is not from the offspring of Aaron should come near to burn incense before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and not be like Korah and like his company, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to him by the hand of Moses.
en.B: as a reminder to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} that no outsider, no one who is not a descendant of Aaron, should come near to burn incense before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, or he would become like Korah and his company. This was done as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Eleazar through Moses.
en.R: This was a reminder to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Only Aaron's descendants may come near to burn incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Anyone else who does this will end up like Korah and his followers. Eleazar did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him through Moses.

es.L: un recordatorio para los hijos de Israel, para que ningún extraño que no sea de la descendencia de Aarón se acerque a quemar incienso delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y no sea como Coré y como su grupo, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había dicho por mano de Moisés.
es.B: como recordatorio para los israelitas de que ningún extraño, nadie que no sea descendiente de Aarón, debe acercarse a quemar incienso delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, o le pasaría lo mismo que a Coré y a su grupo. Esto se hizo como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se lo había indicado a Eleazar por medio de Moisés.
es.R: Esto era un recordatorio para los israelitas. Solo los descendientes de Aarón pueden acercarse a quemar incienso para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Cualquier otra persona que lo haga terminará como Coré y sus seguidores. Eleazar hizo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había dicho por medio de Moisés.

fr.L: un mémorial pour les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, afin qu’aucun profane qui n’est pas de la descendance d’Aaron ne s’approche pour brûler l’encens devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et ne soit comme Coré et comme sa bande, ainsi que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui avait dit par la main de Moïse.
fr.B: comme rappel pour les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} qu’aucun profane, personne qui ne descende d’Aaron, ne doit s’approcher pour brûler de l’encens devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sinon il deviendrait comme Coré et sa bande. Cela fut fait comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit à Éléazar par l’intermédiaire de Moïse.
fr.R: C’était un rappel pour les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Seuls les descendants d’Aaron peuvent s’approcher pour brûler de l’encens devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Toute autre personne qui le fait finira comme Coré et ses partisans. Éléazar a fait ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait dit par Moïse.

sw.L: ukumbusho kwa wana wa Israeli, ili mtu wa nje asiye wa uzao wa Haruni asikaribie kufukiza uvumba mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wala asiwe kama Kora na kama kundi lake, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwambia kwa mkono wa Musa.
sw.B: kuwa ukumbusho kwa Waisraeli kwamba mtu wa nje, yeyote asiye mzao wa Haruni, asikaribie kufukiza uvumba mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, la sivyo atakuwa kama Kora na kundi lake. Hili lilifanyika kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwambia Eleazari kupitia Musa.
sw.R: Huu ulikuwa ukumbusho kwa Waisraeli. Wazao wa Haruni peke yao ndio wanaoweza kukaribia kumfukizia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} uvumba. Mtu mwingine yeyote atakayefanya hivyo ataishia kama Kora na wafuasi wake. Eleazari alifanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwambia kupitia Musa.

decisions.choice: an outsider who is not of Aaron's offspring: anyone outside the priestly family, Levites included
decisions.reason: The word means one who does not belong, here to the priesthood. Korah was a Levite (16:1, 8-10), yet he was an "outsider" to this duty, which belonged to Aaron's descendants alone (3:10; 18:7).

decisions.choice: his company: Korah's band of followers
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the whole congregation of Israel, but here it names the group that gathered around Korah (16:5, 6, 11, 16).

decisions.choice: to him: to Eleazar
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the order about the censers to Eleazar through Moses (verse 2). "Him" most naturally refers back to Eleazar, the one who did the work (verse 4).

decisions.choice: by the hand of Moses: through Moses
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means by means of someone, here Moses as the one who passed on the LORD's word (4:37; Exodus 9:35).

decisions.choice: Eleazar
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Eleazar, whom "him" refers to.

decisions.choice: Only Aaron's descendants may come near
decisions.reason: Readable turns the negative purpose clause into a plain statement of who may burn incense, which means the same.

records.literal_gloss: And grumbled all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel on the next day against Moses and against Aaron, saying, you, you have killed the people of Yahweh.

en.L: And all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel grumbled on the next day against Moses and against Aaron, saying, "You, you have killed the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!"
en.B: The very next day the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} grumbled against Moses and Aaron. "You have killed the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!" they said.
en.R: The next day the whole community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} complained against Moses and Aaron. They said, "You two have killed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people!"

es.L: Y toda la comunidad de los hijos de Israel murmuró al día siguiente contra Moisés y contra Aarón, diciendo: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, {{plural_you:ustedes han matado|vosotros habéis matado}} al pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!».
es.B: Al día siguiente, toda la comunidad de los israelitas murmuró contra Moisés y Aarón. «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes han matado|Habéis matado}} al pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!», decían.
es.R: Al día siguiente, toda la comunidad de los israelitas se quejó contra Moisés y Aarón. Les dijeron: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes dos han matado|Vosotros dos habéis matado}} al pueblo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!».

fr.L: Et toute la communauté des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël murmura le lendemain contre Moïse et contre Aaron, disant : « Vous, vous avez tué le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! »
fr.B: Dès le lendemain, toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} murmura contre Moïse et Aaron. « Vous avez fait mourir le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! » dirent-ils.
fr.R: Le lendemain, toute la communauté des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} s’est plainte de Moïse et d’Aaron. Ils ont dit : « Vous deux, vous avez tué le peuple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! »

sw.L: Na jumuiya yote ya wana wa Israeli ikanung'unika siku iliyofuata juu ya Musa na juu ya Haruni, ikisema, "Ninyi, ninyi mmewaua watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!"
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli iliwanung'unikia Musa na Haruni. Walisema, "Ninyi mmewaua watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!"
sw.R: Kesho yake jumuiya yote ya Waisraeli ililalamika juu ya Musa na Haruni. Walisema, "Ninyi wawili mmewaua watu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!"

decisions.choice: grumbled: complained in bitter protest
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for Israel's complaints in the wilderness (14:2; Exodus 16:2). The people turn against Moses and Aaron again, only a day after the judgment of chapter 16.

decisions.choice: you, you have killed: the blame is put on Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "you" first, as an accusation: it is you who did this. The people blame Moses and Aaron for the deaths of Korah and his followers (16:31-35), though it was the LORD who acted.

decisions.choice: the people of the LORD: the rebels called God's own people
decisions.reason: The congregation calls those who died "the people of the LORD", the very claim Korah made for the whole congregation (16:3). Moses had said the earth opening would show that these men had despised the LORD (16:30).

decisions.choice: You two
decisions.reason: "You" is plural in the Hebrew. Readable says "you two" to show that both Moses and Aaron are blamed.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהִקָּהֵ֤ל הָֽעֵדָה֙ עַל־מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְעַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּפְנוּ֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִנֵּ֥ה כִסָּ֖הוּ הֶעָנָ֑ן וַיֵּרָ֖א כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when assembled the congregation against Moses and against Aaron, and they turned toward [the] tent of meeting, and look, covered it the cloud, and appeared [the] glory of Yahweh.

en.L: And it happened, when the congregation assembled against Moses and against Aaron, that they turned toward the tent of meeting, and look, the cloud covered it, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared.
en.B: But when the congregation gathered against Moses and Aaron and they turned toward the tent of meeting, they saw that the cloud covered it, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared.
en.R: The community gathered to oppose Moses and Aaron. But when they looked toward the meeting tent, the cloud was covering it, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando la comunidad se reunió contra Moisés y contra Aarón, se volvieron hacia la Tienda del Encuentro, y he aquí, la nube la cubría, y apareció la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Pero cuando la comunidad se reunió contra Moisés y Aarón y se volvieron hacia la Tienda del Encuentro, vieron que la nube la cubría, y apareció la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: La comunidad se reunió para oponerse a Moisés y Aarón. Pero cuando miraron hacia la Tienda del Encuentro, la nube la estaba cubriendo, y apareció la gloria {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme la communauté s’assemblait contre Moïse et contre Aaron, qu’ils se tournèrent vers la tente de la Rencontre, et voici, la nuée la couvrait, et la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} apparut.
fr.B: Mais comme la communauté se rassemblait contre Moïse et Aaron et qu’ils se tournaient vers la tente de la Rencontre, ils virent que la nuée la couvrait, et la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} apparut.
fr.R: La communauté s’est rassemblée contre Moïse et Aaron. Mais quand les gens ont regardé vers la tente de la Rencontre, la nuée la couvrait, et la gloire {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} est apparue.

sw.L: Ikawa, jumuiya ilipokusanyika dhidi ya Musa na dhidi ya Haruni, wakageuka kuelekea Hema la Kukutania, na tazama, wingu likalifunika, na utukufu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukaonekana.
sw.B: Lakini jumuiya ilipokusanyika dhidi ya Musa na Haruni, na walipogeuka kuelekea Hema la Kukutania, waliona wingu limelifunika, na utukufu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukaonekana.
sw.R: Jumuiya ilikusanyika kuwapinga Musa na Haruni. Lakini walipotazama upande wa Hema la Kukutania, wingu lilikuwa limelifunika, na utukufu wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukaonekana.

decisions.choice: they turned: most naturally the people, perhaps Moses and Aaron with them
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. The people who had gathered turned to look toward the tent; Moses and Aaron then go to it (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared: God comes to intervene
decisions.reason: The cloud was the sign of the LORD's presence over the tent (9:15-16), and his glory appears when the people rebel, to bring judgment (14:10; 16:19).

decisions.choice: they saw that
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word that points to something seen is given as "look" in Literal; Balanced says what it means here, that they saw it.

es.R: Moisés y Aarón fueron y se pararon delante de la Tienda del Encuentro.

fr.R: Moïse et Aaron sont allés se tenir devant la tente de la Rencontre.

sw.B: Musa na Haruni walikuja mbele ya Hema la Kukutania,
sw.R: Musa na Haruni walikwenda wakasimama mbele ya Hema la Kukutania.

decisions.choice: the front of the tent of meeting: the open court before its entrance
decisions.reason: Moses and Aaron go to where the LORD speaks with Moses (Exodus 33:9-11), the place where Aaron later comes back to stand (verse 15).

fr.B: et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} parla à Moïse. Il dit :

sw.B: naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanena na Musa. Akasema,
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa,

decisions.choice: and the LORD said
decisions.reason: Balanced joins verses 8 and 9 into one English sentence, as they follow each other closely.

source.text: הֵרֹ֗מּוּ מִתּוֹךְ֙ הָעֵדָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וַאֲכַלֶּ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם כְּרָ֑גַע וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Get away from [the] midst of the congregation the this, and I will consume them in a moment. And they fell on their faces.

en.L: "Get yourselves away from the midst of this congregation, and I will consume them in a moment." And they fell on their faces.
en.B: "Get away from this congregation, and I will wipe them out in a moment." But they fell face down.
en.R: "Move away from these people, so that I can destroy them right now." But Moses and Aaron threw themselves face down on the ground.

es.L: «{{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} de en medio de esta comunidad, y los consumiré en un momento». Y cayeron sobre sus rostros.
es.B: «{{plural_you:Aléjense|Alejaos}} de esta comunidad, y acabaré con ellos en un instante». Pero ellos se postraron rostro en tierra.
es.R: «{{plural_you:Apártense|Apartaos}} de esta gente, para que yo pueda destruirlos ahora mismo». Pero Moisés y Aarón se tiraron al suelo, con el rostro en tierra.

fr.L: « Retirez-vous du milieu de cette communauté, et je les consumerai en un instant. » Et ils tombèrent sur leurs faces.
fr.B: « Écartez-vous de cette communauté, et je les anéantirai en un instant. » Mais ils se jetèrent face contre terre.
fr.R: « Éloignez-vous de ces gens, pour que je puisse les détruire tout de suite. » Mais Moïse et Aaron se sont jetés face contre terre.

sw.L: "Jiondoeni kutoka katikati ya jumuiya hii, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawakomesha mara moja." Nao wakaanguka kwa nyuso zao.
sw.B: "Ondokeni mbali na jumuiya hii, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawaangamiza papo hapo." Lakini wao wakaanguka kifudifudi.
sw.R: "Kaeni mbali na watu hawa, ili niwaangamize sasa hivi." Lakini Musa na Haruni walijitupa chini kifudifudi.

decisions.choice: get away ... and I will consume them in a moment: the words of 16:21 again
decisions.reason: The LORD said almost the same to Moses and Aaron the day before (16:21). Then too they fell on their faces and pleaded for the people (16:22).

decisions.choice: consume: put an end to, wipe out
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something to an end, to finish it off. It is the threat of 16:21 and of the golden calf (Exodus 32:10).

decisions.choice: they fell on their faces: they lay face down in appeal to God
decisions.reason: Falling on the face is a gesture of humility and pleading (14:5; 16:4, 22). Moses and Aaron do not leave the people but turn to God for them.

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins with "and". Balanced and Readable say "but", since Moses and Aaron do not move away as told; they fall down and intercede.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names who fell down.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֣ח אֶת־הַ֠מַּחְתָּה וְתֶן־עָלֶ֨יהָ אֵ֜שׁ מֵעַ֤ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ וְשִׂ֣ים קְטֹ֔רֶת וְהוֹלֵ֧ךְ מְהֵרָ֛ה אֶל־הָעֵדָ֖ה וְכַפֵּ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־יָצָ֥א הַקֶּ֛צֶף מִלִּפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֵחֵ֥ל הַנָּֽגֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, take the censer and put on it fire from on the altar and set incense, and carry quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them; for has gone out the wrath from before Yahweh, has begun the plague.

en.L: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take the censer and put fire on it from on the altar, and set incense [on it], and carry [it] quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them; for the wrath has gone out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; the plague has begun."
en.B: Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer, put fire in it from the altar, and lay incense on it. Then take it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because wrath has gone out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The plague has begun!"
en.R: Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer. Put burning coals from the altar in it, and put incense on the coals. Then hurry to the people and make atonement for them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is angry, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} punishment has already begun. A plague has started!"

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a Aarón: «Toma el incensario y pon en él fuego de sobre el altar, y pon incienso [encima], y lleva[lo] pronto a la comunidad y haz expiación por ellos; porque la ira ha salido de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; la plaga ha comenzado».
es.B: Moisés le dijo a Aarón: «Toma tu incensario, ponle fuego del altar y echa incienso encima. Luego llévalo pronto a la comunidad y haz expiación por ellos, porque la ira ha salido de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. ¡La plaga ha comenzado!».
es.R: Moisés le dijo a Aarón: «Toma tu incensario. Pon en él brasas del altar y echa incienso sobre las brasas. Luego ve corriendo hacia la gente y haz expiación por ellos. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} está enojado, y {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} castigo ya ha comenzado. ¡Ha empezado una plaga!».

fr.L: Et Moïse dit à Aaron : « Prends l’encensoir et mets dessus du feu de dessus l’autel, et pose de l’encens [dessus], et porte[-le] vite vers la communauté et fais l’expiation pour eux ; car la colère est sortie de devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; le fléau a commencé. »
fr.B: Moïse dit à Aaron : « Prends ton encensoir, mets-y du feu pris sur l’autel, et dépose de l’encens dessus. Puis porte-le vite vers la communauté et fais l’expiation pour eux, car la colère est sortie de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Le fléau a commencé ! »
fr.R: Moïse a dit à Aaron : « Prends ton encensoir. Mets dedans des braises prises sur l’autel, et mets de l’encens sur les braises. Ensuite, va vite vers les gens et fais l’expiation pour eux. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est en colère, et {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} punition a déjà commencé. Un fléau s’est déclaré ! »

sw.L: Naye Musa akamwambia Haruni, "Chukua chetezo, utie ndani yake moto kutoka juu ya madhabahu, na uweke uvumba [juu yake], na upeleke [chetezo] upesi kwa jumuiya, ufanye upatanisho kwa ajili yao; kwa maana ghadhabu imetoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; pigo limeanza."
sw.B: Musa akamwambia Haruni, "Chukua chetezo chako, utie ndani yake moto kutoka madhabahuni, na uweke uvumba juu yake. Kisha ukipeleke upesi kwa jumuiya, ukawafanyie upatanisho, kwa sababu ghadhabu imetoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Pigo limeanza!"
sw.R: Musa akamwambia Haruni, "Chukua chetezo chako. Tia ndani yake makaa ya moto kutoka madhabahuni, kisha uweke uvumba juu ya makaa hayo. Halafu nenda haraka kwa watu, ukawafanyie upatanisho. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekasirika, na adhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} imeshaanza. Pigo limeanza!"

decisions.choice: the censer: Aaron's own censer as high priest
decisions.reason: The article points to a censer known to them: the one Aaron carried before the LORD the day before (16:17-18).

decisions.choice: fire from on the altar: coals from the altar of burnt offering
decisions.reason: The incense was to be burned on coals from the altar where the LORD's fire burned (Leviticus 16:12), not on fire taken from anywhere else, as Nadab and Abihu had done (Leviticus 10:1).

decisions.choice: incense and atonement: the offering that brought death to the 250 now saves the people
decisions.reason: Atonement was usually made with blood (Leviticus 17:11). Here the high priest makes atonement with incense. The same act that the 250 men had no right to do, and that killed them (16:35), when done by the priest God chose, stops the plague. It answers the people's charge against Aaron (16:11).

decisions.choice: the wrath has gone out from before the LORD: God's anger has begun to act
decisions.reason: God's wrath is pictured as going out from his presence like a force sent against the people (1:53; 18:5). The plague is that wrath at work.

decisions.choice: the plague: a blow, a deadly striking
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to strike. It names a sudden deadly blow sent by God (Exodus 12:13). Verses 13-15 use a related word from the same root.

decisions.choice: your censer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "your" for the Hebrew "the", since it is the censer Aaron already had.

decisions.choice: The LORD is angry, and his punishment has already begun
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of wrath going out means.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀דִּבֶּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיָּ֨רָץ֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךהַקָּהָ֔ל וְהִנֵּ֛ה הֵחֵ֥ל הַנֶּ֖גֶף בָּעָ֑ם וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶֽת־הַקְּטֹ֔רֶת וַיְכַפֵּ֖ר עַל־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took Aaron as had spoken Moses, and ran into [the] midst of the assembly, and look, had begun the plague among the people; and he put on the incense and made atonement for the people.

en.L: And Aaron took [it] as Moses had spoken, and ran into the midst of the assembly, and look, the plague had begun among the people; and he put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
en.B: So Aaron took it as Moses had said and ran into the middle of the assembly. The plague had already begun among the people, but he put the incense on and made atonement for them.
en.R: So Aaron did what Moses said. He ran into the middle of the crowd. People were already dying from the plague. Aaron put the incense on the coals and made atonement for them.

es.L: Y Aarón [lo] tomó como Moisés había dicho, y corrió al medio de la asamblea, y he aquí, la plaga había comenzado en el pueblo; y puso el incienso e hizo expiación por el pueblo.
es.B: Así que Aarón lo tomó como Moisés había dicho y corrió al medio de la asamblea. La plaga ya había comenzado entre el pueblo, pero él puso el incienso e hizo expiación por ellos.
es.R: Entonces Aarón hizo lo que Moisés le dijo. Corrió al medio de la multitud. La gente ya estaba muriendo por la plaga. Aarón puso el incienso sobre las brasas e hizo expiación por ellos.

fr.L: Et Aaron [le] prit comme Moïse l’avait dit, et courut au milieu de l’assemblée, et voici, le fléau avait commencé parmi le peuple ; et il mit l’encens et fit l’expiation pour le peuple.
fr.B: Aaron le prit donc, comme Moïse l’avait dit, et courut au milieu de l’assemblée. Le fléau avait déjà commencé parmi le peuple, mais il mit l’encens et fit l’expiation pour eux.
fr.R: Aaron a donc fait ce que Moïse avait dit. Il a couru au milieu de la foule. Des gens mouraient déjà du fléau. Aaron a mis l’encens sur les braises et il a fait l’expiation pour eux.

sw.L: Naye Haruni akakichukua kama Musa alivyosema, akakimbia katikati ya kusanyiko, na tazama, pigo lilikuwa limeanza kati ya watu; naye akaweka uvumba, akafanya upatanisho kwa ajili ya watu.
sw.B: Basi Haruni akakichukua kama Musa alivyosema, akakimbia katikati ya kusanyiko. Pigo lilikuwa limekwisha kuanza kati ya watu, lakini yeye akaweka uvumba na kuwafanyia upatanisho.
sw.R: Basi Haruni alifanya kama Musa alivyosema. Alikimbia katikati ya umati wa watu. Watu walikuwa tayari wanakufa kwa pigo hilo. Haruni aliweka uvumba juu ya makaa, akawafanyia upatanisho.

decisions.choice: the assembly: the people gathered together
decisions.reason: The word for a gathered assembly is used here alongside "congregation" (verse 11) for the same crowd that had gathered against Moses and Aaron (verse 7).

decisions.choice: he ran and made atonement: the high priest acts at once for the people
decisions.reason: Aaron, the man the people had just accused, runs into the crowd where the plague is striking and makes atonement for them. His act shows that he is the priest God has chosen to stand for the people (16:5; 17:20).

decisions.choice: People were already dying from the plague
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the plague had begun" meant for those in the crowd.

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד בֵּֽין־הַמֵּתִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַֽחַיִּ֑ים וַתֵּעָצַ֖ר הַמַּגֵּפָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he stood between the dead and between the living, and was stopped the plague.

en.L: And he stood between the dead and between the living, and the plague was stopped.
en.B: He took his stand between the dead and the living, and the plague was held back.
en.R: He stood between those who had died and those who were still alive, and the plague stopped.

es.L: Y se puso de pie entre los muertos y entre los vivos, y la plaga se detuvo.
es.B: Se plantó entre los muertos y los vivos, y la plaga fue contenida.
es.R: Se quedó de pie entre los que habían muerto y los que seguían vivos, y la plaga se detuvo.

fr.L: Et il se tint entre les morts et entre les vivants, et le fléau fut arrêté.
fr.B: Il se plaça entre les morts et les vivants, et le fléau fut retenu.
fr.R: Il s’est tenu entre ceux qui étaient morts et ceux qui étaient encore vivants, et le fléau s’est arrêté.

sw.L: Naye akasimama kati ya wafu na kati ya walio hai, na pigo likazuiliwa.
sw.B: Alisimama imara kati ya wafu na walio hai, na pigo likazuiliwa.
sw.R: Alisimama kati ya wale waliokufa na wale waliokuwa bado hai, na pigo likakoma.

decisions.choice: he stood between the dead and the living: the priest stands in the gap for the people
decisions.reason: Aaron places himself, with the incense, at the edge of the plague's advance. The picture is of a man who stands between God's judgment and the people, as Moses did in Psalm 106:23.

decisions.choice: the plague was stopped: it was held back and ended
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold back or restrain. The word for "plague" here is related to the one in verses 11-12; both come from a verb meaning to strike, and both name the same blow. The plague of Psalm 106:30, also "stopped", uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: those who died over the matter of Korah: Korah, Dathan, Abiram and the 250
decisions.reason: These are the men swallowed by the earth with their households (16:31-33) and the 250 consumed by fire (16:35).

decisions.choice: because of Korah / because of what Korah did

sw.B: Kisha Haruni akarudi kwa Musa mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania, kwa maana pigo lilikuwa limezuiliwa.

decisions.choice: and the plague had been stopped: the reason Aaron could return
decisions.reason: The last clause tells the state of things when Aaron came back: the plague was over. It closes the account and explains why Aaron could leave the people.

decisions.reason: Balanced makes the link explicit with "for".

decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does, where chapter 17 began with the censers and the plague (17:1-15 here). Many Bibles number those verses 16:36-50 and begin chapter 17 here, so 17:16 here is 17:1 there, and 17:28 here is 17:13 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel, and take from them a staff, a staff for [each] house of [a] father, from all their leaders, by [the] house of their fathers, twelve staffs; [each] man his name you will write on his staff.

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and take from them a staff, a staff for each father's house, from all their leaders by their fathers' houses, twelve staffs. You shall write each man's name on his staff.
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and get a staff from them for each ancestral family, one from each of their leaders by their ancestral families: twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his staff.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to give you twelve walking sticks, one from the leader of each tribe. Write each leader's name on his own stick.

es.L: «Habla a los hijos de Israel, y toma de ellos una vara, una vara por cada casa paterna, de todos sus jefes según la casa de sus padres, doce varas. Escribirás el nombre de cada uno sobre su vara.
es.B: «Habla a los israelitas y consigue de ellos una vara por cada familia de sus antepasados, una de cada uno de sus jefes según sus familias: doce varas. Escribe el nombre de cada uno en su vara.
es.R: «Dile a los israelitas que te den doce bastones, uno del jefe de cada tribu. Escribe el nombre de cada jefe en su propio bastón.

sw.L: "Nena na wana wa Israeli, uchukue kutoka kwao fimbo, fimbo moja kwa kila nyumba ya baba, kutoka kwa viongozi wao wote kwa nyumba ya baba zao, fimbo kumi na mbili. Utaandika jina la kila mtu juu ya fimbo yake.
sw.B: "Sema na Waisraeli, upate kutoka kwao fimbo moja kwa kila jamaa ya mababu, moja kutoka kwa kila kiongozi wao kwa jamaa zao: fimbo kumi na mbili. Andika jina la kila mtu juu ya fimbo yake.
sw.R: "Waambie Waisraeli wakupe fimbo kumi na mbili, moja kutoka kwa kiongozi wa kila kabila. Andika jina la kila kiongozi juu ya fimbo yake mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: staff: a wooden staff or rod, and the same word as "tribe"
decisions.reason: The word means a staff, the stick a leader or shepherd carried as a sign of his place (Genesis 38:18; Exodus 4:2). The same word also means "tribe", the group that such a leader headed (1:4, 16). The chapter plays on both: each tribe is represented by its leader's staff, and the LORD will show which tribe he has chosen by what happens to its staff.

decisions.choice: a father's house: here a whole tribe
decisions.reason: A "father's house" is usually a family within a clan (1:2). Here it names each tribe as the house of its ancestor, since there is one staff for each of the twelve and each is given by the tribe's leader (verse 21; 1:4, 16).

decisions.choice: their leaders: the twelve tribal leaders
decisions.reason: These are the leaders of the tribes named in 1:5-16 and 7:12-83, who stood for their whole tribe.

decisions.choice: walking sticks / stick
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for the leaders' staffs, the sticks they carried.

decisions.choice: the leader of each tribe
decisions.reason: Readable says "tribe" for "father's house", which is what it means here.

records.literal_gloss: And [the] name of Aaron you will write on [the] staff of Levi; for one staff [is] for [the] head of [the] house of their fathers.

en.L: And you shall write the name of Aaron on the staff of Levi, for one staff [is] for the head of their fathers' house.
en.B: On Levi's staff you are to write Aaron's name, because each head of an ancestral family has one staff.
en.R: Write Aaron's name on the stick for the tribe of Levi. The leader of every tribe gets one stick.

es.L: Y escribirás el nombre de Aarón sobre la vara de Leví, porque una sola vara [es] para la cabeza de la casa de sus padres.
es.B: En la vara de Leví escribirás el nombre de Aarón, porque cada jefe de familia ancestral tiene una sola vara.
es.R: Escribe el nombre de Aarón en el bastón de la tribu de Leví. El jefe de cada tribu recibe un bastón.

fr.L: Et tu écriras le nom d’Aaron sur le bâton de Lévi, car un seul bâton [est] pour le chef de la maison de leurs pères.
fr.B: Sur le bâton de Lévi, tu écriras le nom d’Aaron, car chaque chef de famille ancestrale a un seul bâton.
fr.R: Écris le nom d’Aaron sur le bâton de la tribu de Lévi. Le chef de chaque tribu reçoit un bâton.

sw.L: Na utaandika jina la Haruni juu ya fimbo ya Lawi, kwa maana fimbo moja [ni] kwa ajili ya mkuu wa nyumba ya baba zao.
sw.B: Juu ya fimbo ya Lawi utaandika jina la Haruni, kwa sababu kila mkuu wa jamaa ya mababu ana fimbo moja.
sw.R: Andika jina la Haruni juu ya fimbo ya kabila la Lawi. Kiongozi wa kila kabila anapata fimbo moja.

decisions.choice: Aaron's name on the staff of Levi: Aaron stands as the head of the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: Korah, a Levite, had challenged Aaron's place (16:1-11). Writing Aaron's name on Levi's staff puts him forward as the head of that tribe, the one the test is about.

decisions.choice: one staff for the head of their fathers' house: one staff for each tribal head
decisions.reason: The clause gives the reason for the rule: each tribe has one staff, carrying its head's name. Levi is no exception, and its one staff bears Aaron's name.

decisions.choice: each head (Balanced); every tribe (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the rule of one staff applies to every tribe, Levi included.

source.text: וְהִנַּחְתָּ֖ם בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד לִפְנֵי֙ הָֽעֵד֔וּת אֲשֶׁ֛ר אִוָּעֵ֥ד לָכֶ֖ם שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will deposit them in [the] tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you there.

en.L: And you shall deposit them in the tent of meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you there.
en.B: Then place them in the tent of meeting in front of the testimony, where I meet with you.
en.R: Then put them in the meeting tent, in front of the ark that holds the covenant tablets. That is where I meet with you.

es.L: Y las depositarás en la Tienda del Encuentro delante del Testimonio, donde me encuentro con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} allí.
es.B: Luego colócalas en la Tienda del Encuentro, delante del Testimonio, donde me encuentro con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Después ponlos en la Tienda del Encuentro, delante del arca que guarda las tablas del pacto. Allí es donde me encuentro con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et tu les déposeras dans la tente de la Rencontre devant le Témoignage, où je vous rencontre là.
fr.B: Puis place-les dans la tente de la Rencontre, devant le Témoignage, là où je vous rencontre.
fr.R: Ensuite, mets-les dans la tente de la Rencontre, devant l’arche qui contient les tablettes de l’alliance. C’est là que je vous rencontre.

sw.L: Nawe utaziweka katika Hema la Kukutania mbele ya Ushuhuda, ambapo ninakutana nanyi huko.
sw.B: Kisha uziweke ndani ya Hema la Kukutania mbele ya Ushuhuda, ninapokutana nanyi.
sw.R: Kisha uziweke ndani ya Hema la Kukutania, mbele ya sanduku lenye vibao vya agano. Hapo ndipo ninapokutana nanyi.

decisions.choice: the testimony: the covenant tablets kept in the ark
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the two stone tablets of the covenant, placed inside the ark in the most holy place (Exodus 25:16, 21; 31:18). "Before the testimony" means in front of the ark (Exodus 16:34; 27:21).

decisions.choice: where I meet with you: the place God promised to meet Israel
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised to meet with Moses and the people at the ark and the tent (Exodus 25:22; 29:42; 30:36). The tent is called the tent of meeting for this reason. "You" is plural here.

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the testimony" as the ark with the tablets, as it does for "the ark of the testimony".

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֶבְחַר־בּ֖וֹ מַטֵּ֣הוּ יִפְרָ֑ח וַהֲשִׁכֹּתִ֣י מֵֽעָלַ֗י אֶת־תְּלֻנּוֹת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם מַלִּינִ֖ם עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be [that] the man whom I choose him, his staff will sprout; and I will make subside from upon me the grumblings of [the] sons of Israel which they [are] grumbling against you.

en.L: And it shall be that the man whom I choose, his staff will sprout; and I will make the grumblings of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, which they are grumbling against you, subside from upon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: The man I choose is the one whose staff will sprout. So I will make the grumbling of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} against you die down, and it will trouble {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no more."
en.R: The stick of the man I choose will start to grow leaves. Then I will put an end to the way the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} keep complaining to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about you."

es.L: Y sucederá que el hombre que yo escoja, su vara brotará; y haré cesar de sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} las murmuraciones de los hijos de Israel, que ellos murmuran contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».
es.B: El hombre que yo escoja será aquel cuya vara brote. Así haré que se calmen las murmuraciones de los israelitas contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y ya no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} molestarán más».
es.R: Al bastón del hombre que yo escoja le saldrán hojas. Entonces pondré fin a las quejas que los israelitas siempre {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} presentan contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}».

fr.L: Et il arrivera que l’homme que je choisirai, son bâton bourgeonnera ; et je ferai cesser de dessus {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} les murmures des {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, qu’ils murmurent contre vous. »
fr.B: L’homme que je choisirai sera celui dont le bâton bourgeonnera. Ainsi j’apaiserai les murmures des {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} contre vous, et ils ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pèseront plus. »
fr.R: Le bâton de l’homme que je choisirai va se couvrir de feuilles. Alors je mettrai fin aux plaintes que les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}adressent sans cesse contre vous. »

sw.L: Na itakuwa kwamba mtu yule nitakayemchagua, fimbo yake itachipuka; {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitayakomesha kutoka juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} manung'uniko ya wana wa Israeli, wanayowanung'unikia ninyi."
sw.B: Mtu nitakayemchagua ndiye ambaye fimbo yake itachipuka. Hivyo nitayatuliza manung'uniko ya Waisraeli dhidi yenu, wala hayatanisumbua tena."
sw.R: Fimbo ya mtu nitakayemchagua itaanza kutoa majani. Ndipo nitakapokomesha malalamiko ambayo Waisraeli huyaleta {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kila mara juu yenu."

decisions.choice: the man whom I choose: God himself will show who is his priest
decisions.reason: Korah had claimed that the whole congregation was holy (16:3), and Moses had said that the LORD would show whom he chose (16:5, 7). The sign settles the question for good: the choice is God's, not Aaron's or Moses'.

decisions.choice: sprout: put out shoots
decisions.reason: The verb means to bud or break out in growth. A dead staff cut from a tree has no power to grow, so its sprouting could only be God's doing. Verse 23 tells how far beyond sprouting it went.

decisions.choice: make subside from upon me: quiet the complaints and lift them off me
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something sink down or abate. It is used of floodwaters going down (Genesis 8:1). The grumbling against Moses and Aaron is treated as grumbling that rises up against God himself.

decisions.choice: against you: against Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: "You" is plural, as in 16:11 and 17:6, where the people grumbled against both of them.

decisions.choice: make ... die down, and it will trouble me no more (Balanced); put an end to the way ... keep complaining (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the grumbling sinking down and says what "from upon me" means: it will no longer weigh on God. The Hebrew uses a participle for the grumbling, something the people keep doing; Readable brings that out with "keep".

decisions.choice: start to grow leaves
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain picture for "sprout".

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֵלָ֣יו׀כָּֽל־נְשִֽׂיאֵיהֶ֡ם מַטֶּה֩ לְנָשִׂ֨יא אֶחָ֜ד מַטֶּ֨ה לְנָשִׂ֤יא אֶחָד֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֔ם שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר מַטּ֑וֹת וּמַטֵּ֥ה אַהֲרֹ֖ן בְּת֥וֹךְ מַטּוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Moses to [the] sons of Israel, and gave to him all their leaders a staff for leader one, a staff for leader one, by [the] house of their fathers, twelve staffs; and [the] staff of Aaron [was] in [the] midst of their staffs.

en.L: And Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one staff for each leader, by their fathers' houses, twelve staffs; and the staff of Aaron [was] among their staffs.
en.B: So Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one for each leader, by their ancestral families: twelve staffs. Aaron's staff was among them.
en.R: So Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Each of the twelve tribal leaders gave him a stick, and Aaron's stick was with theirs.

es.L: Y habló Moisés a los hijos de Israel, y todos sus jefes le dieron una vara, una vara por cada jefe, según la casa de sus padres, doce varas; y la vara de Aarón [estaba] en medio de las varas de ellos.
es.B: Así que Moisés habló a los israelitas, y todos sus jefes le dieron varas, una por cada jefe, según sus familias ancestrales: doce varas. La vara de Aarón estaba entre ellas.
es.R: Entonces Moisés habló con los israelitas. Cada uno de los doce jefes de tribu le dio un bastón, y el bastón de Aarón estaba con los de ellos.

fr.L: Et Moïse parla aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël, et tous leurs chefs lui donnèrent un bâton, un bâton par chef, selon la maison de leurs pères, douze bâtons ; et le bâton d’Aaron [était] au milieu de leurs bâtons.
fr.B: Moïse parla donc aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}, et tous leurs chefs lui donnèrent des bâtons, un par chef, selon leurs familles ancestrales : douze bâtons. Le bâton d’Aaron était parmi eux.
fr.R: Moïse a donc parlé aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Chacun des douze chefs de tribu lui a donné un bâton, et le bâton d’Aaron était avec les leurs.

sw.L: Naye Musa akanena na wana wa Israeli, na viongozi wao wote wakampa fimbo, fimbo moja kwa kila kiongozi, kwa nyumba ya baba zao, fimbo kumi na mbili; na fimbo ya Haruni [ilikuwa] katikati ya fimbo zao.
sw.B: Basi Musa akasema na Waisraeli, na viongozi wao wote wakampa fimbo, moja kwa kila kiongozi, kwa jamaa za mababu zao: fimbo kumi na mbili. Fimbo ya Haruni ilikuwa miongoni mwa fimbo hizo.
sw.R: Basi Musa alisema na Waisraeli. Kila mmoja wa viongozi kumi na wawili wa makabila alimpa fimbo, na fimbo ya Haruni ilikuwa pamoja na fimbo zao.

decisions.choice: twelve staffs, and Aaron's among them: Aaron's staff may be one of the twelve or a thirteenth
alternatives: twelve staffs, with Aaron's staff in addition to them
decisions.reason: The text can mean that Aaron's staff was one of the twelve, with Joseph counted as one tribe, or that there were twelve staffs of the other tribes, with Ephraim and Manasseh counted separately, and Aaron's staff among them. Verse 18 speaks of Levi's staff as one of the tribes' staffs, which favors the first reading. The point is the same either way: Aaron's staff was tested alongside the others.

decisions.choice: a staff for one leader, a staff for one leader: one staff for each leader
decisions.reason: Saying the phrase twice is the Hebrew way of saying "each" (compare 13:2).

decisions.choice: Each of the twelve tribal leaders gave him a stick
decisions.reason: Readable puts the number with the leaders and leaves out the repeated phrases, which mean the same.

source.text: וַיַּנַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־הַמַּטֹּ֖ת לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּאֹ֖הֶל הָעֵדֻֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And deposited Moses the staffs before Yahweh in [the] tent of the testimony.

en.L: And Moses deposited the staffs before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the tent of the testimony.
en.B: Moses placed the staffs before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the tent of the testimony.
en.R: Moses put the sticks in the tent where the covenant tablets were kept. There they were in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y Moisés depositó las varas delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en la Tienda del Testimonio.
es.B: Moisés colocó las varas delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en la Tienda del Testimonio.
es.R: Moisés puso los bastones en la tienda donde se guardaban las tablas del pacto. Allí quedaron, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et Moïse déposa les bâtons devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dans la tente du Témoignage.
fr.B: Moïse plaça les bâtons devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dans la tente du Témoignage.
fr.R: Moïse a mis les bâtons dans la tente où étaient gardées les tablettes de l’alliance. Ils étaient là, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Naye Musa akaziweka fimbo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika Hema la Ushuhuda.
sw.B: Musa aliziweka fimbo hizo mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndani ya Hema la Ushuhuda.
sw.R: Musa aliziweka fimbo ndani ya hema ambamo vibao vya agano vilitunzwa. Huko zilikuwa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: the tent of the testimony: the tent of meeting, which held the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: The tent is named after the testimony kept in it (1:50, 53; 9:15). Laying the staffs before the testimony (verse 19) is laying them "before the LORD".

decisions.choice: the tent where the covenant tablets were kept
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name of the tent, as in 9:15.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַיָּבֹ֤א מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל הָעֵד֔וּת וְהִנֵּ֛ה פָּרַ֥ח מַטֵּֽה־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לְבֵ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיֹּ֤צֵֽא פֶ֨רַח֙ וַיָּ֣צֵֽץ צִ֔יץ וַיִּגְמֹ֖ל שְׁקֵדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on the next day, and went Moses into [the] tent of the testimony, and look, had sprouted [the] staff of Aaron for [the] house of Levi, and it brought out buds, and blossomed blossom[s], and ripened almonds.

en.L: And it happened on the next day that Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and look, the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi had sprouted; and it had brought out buds and blossomed blossoms and ripened almonds.
en.B: The next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and there was Aaron's staff, the staff for the house of Levi, sprouting. It had put out buds, opened into blossoms, and borne ripe almonds.
en.R: The next day Moses went into the tent. He saw that Aaron's stick, the one for the tribe of Levi, had come to life. It had grown buds and flowers, and it even had ripe almonds on it!

es.L: Y sucedió al día siguiente que Moisés entró en la Tienda del Testimonio, y he aquí, la vara de Aarón por la casa de Leví había brotado; y había echado brotes y florecido flores y madurado almendras.
es.B: Al día siguiente Moisés entró en la Tienda del Testimonio, y allí estaba la vara de Aarón, la de la casa de Leví, que había brotado. Había echado brotes, se había abierto en flores y tenía almendras maduras.
es.R: Al día siguiente Moisés entró en la tienda. Vio que el bastón de Aarón, el de la tribu de Leví, había vuelto a la vida. Le habían salido brotes y flores, ¡y hasta tenía almendras maduras!

fr.L: Et il arriva le lendemain que Moïse entra dans la tente du Témoignage, et voici, le bâton d’Aaron pour la maison de Lévi avait bourgeonné ; il avait produit des bourgeons, fait éclore des fleurs et mûrir des amandes.
fr.B: Le lendemain, Moïse entra dans la tente du Témoignage, et voici que le bâton d’Aaron, celui de la maison de Lévi, avait bourgeonné. Il avait poussé des bourgeons, s’était couvert de fleurs et portait des amandes mûres.
fr.R: Le lendemain, Moïse est entré dans la tente. Il a vu que le bâton d’Aaron, celui de la tribu de Lévi, avait repris vie. Il avait des bourgeons et des fleurs, et même des amandes mûres !

sw.L: Ikawa siku iliyofuata Musa akaingia katika Hema la Ushuhuda, na tazama, fimbo ya Haruni kwa ajili ya nyumba ya Lawi ilikuwa imechipuka; ilikuwa imetoa machipukizi, ikachanua maua, ikaivisha lozi.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata Musa aliingia ndani ya Hema la Ushuhuda, na hapo ilikuwapo fimbo ya Haruni, fimbo ya nyumba ya Lawi, ikiwa imechipuka. Ilikuwa imetoa machipukizi, imechanua maua, na kuzaa lozi zilizoiva.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata Musa aliingia ndani ya hema. Aliona kwamba fimbo ya Haruni, ile ya kabila la Lawi, ilikuwa imepata uhai tena. Ilikuwa imetoa machipukizi na maua, na hata ilikuwa na lozi zilizoiva!

decisions.choice: sprouted, buds, blossoms and ripe almonds: far more than the sign promised
decisions.reason: The LORD said only that the staff would sprout (verse 20). In one night it went through every stage of growth at once, from buds to flowers to ripe fruit. The sign leaves no doubt.

decisions.choice: almonds: the tree that wakes first
decisions.reason: The almond tree blossoms first in the year. In Jeremiah 1:11-12 its name sounds like the word for "watching", and God says he is watching over his word. The cups of the lampstand in the holy place were shaped like almond blossoms (Exodus 25:33-34).

decisions.choice: the house of Levi: the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: As in verse 17, "house" here means a whole tribe, named after its ancestor Levi.

decisions.choice: there was
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the word that points to what is seen as "there was".

decisions.choice: had come to life
decisions.reason: Readable says what sprouting meant for a dry stick: it had become a living branch again.

source.text: וַיֹּצֵ֨א מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־כָּל־הַמַּטֹּת֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־כָּל־בְּנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּרְא֥וּ וַיִּקְח֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ מַטֵּֽהוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And brought out Moses all the staffs from before Yahweh to all [the] sons of Israel; and they looked, and took each his staff.

en.L: And Moses brought out all the staffs from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; and they looked, and each man took his staff.
en.B: Then Moses brought all the staffs out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They looked at them, and each leader took back his own staff.
en.R: Moses brought all the sticks out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s presence and showed them to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They looked at them, and each leader took back his own stick.

es.L: Y sacó Moisés todas las varas de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} a todos los hijos de Israel; y miraron, y tomaron cada uno su vara.
es.B: Luego Moisés sacó todas las varas de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se las llevó a todos los israelitas. Ellos las miraron, y cada jefe recogió su propia vara.
es.R: Moisés sacó todos los bastones de la presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y se los mostró a todos los israelitas. Ellos los miraron, y cada jefe recogió su propio bastón.

fr.L: Et Moïse sortit tous les bâtons de devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vers tous les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël ; et ils regardèrent, et ils prirent chacun son bâton.
fr.B: Puis Moïse sortit tous les bâtons de devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et les apporta à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Ils les regardèrent, et chaque chef reprit son propre bâton.
fr.R: Moïse a sorti tous les bâtons de la présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et il les a montrés à tous les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}}. Ils les ont regardés, et chaque chef a repris son bâton.

sw.L: Naye Musa akazitoa fimbo zote kutoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa wana wote wa Israeli; nao wakaona, wakachukua kila mtu fimbo yake.
sw.B: Kisha Musa akazitoa fimbo zote kutoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kuzileta kwa Waisraeli wote. Wakaziangalia, na kila kiongozi akachukua fimbo yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Musa alizitoa fimbo zote kutoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akawaonyesha Waisraeli wote. Wakaziangalia, na kila kiongozi akachukua fimbo yake mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: they looked, and each took his staff: the other staffs were unchanged
decisions.reason: Every leader saw his own staff still dry and Aaron's alone in bloom. Each took his own back, so the whole people could see the difference.

decisions.choice: each leader
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "leader", since the staffs belonged to the tribal leaders (verse 21).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הָשֵׁ֞ב אֶת־מַטֵּ֤ה אַהֲרֹן֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָעֵד֔וּת לְמִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת לְא֖וֹת לִבְנֵי־מֶ֑רִי וּתְכַ֧ל תְּלוּנֹּתָ֛ם מֵעָלַ֖י וְלֹ֥א יָמֻֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, put back [the] staff of Aaron before the testimony, for keeping, for a sign to [the] sons of rebellion, that you may end their grumblings from upon me, and they will not die.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Put back the staff of Aaron before the testimony, to be kept as a sign to the sons of rebellion, so that you may put an end to their grumblings from upon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they will not die."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Return Aaron's staff to its place before the testimony. It is to be kept there as a sign for the rebels, so that you can stop their complaints against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and they do not die."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Put Aaron's stick back in front of the ark. Keep it there as a warning sign for those who rebel. This will stop their complaints against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they will not die."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés: «Vuelve a poner la vara de Aarón delante del Testimonio, para que se guarde como señal para los hijos de rebelión, para que acabes con sus murmuraciones de sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y no mueran».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «Devuelve la vara de Aarón a su lugar delante del Testimonio. Allí se guardará como señal para los rebeldes, para que pongas fin a sus quejas contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y no mueran».
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «Pon otra vez el bastón de Aarón delante del arca. Guárdalo allí como una señal de advertencia para los que se rebelan. Esto acabará con sus quejas contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y no morirán».

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Remets le bâton d’Aaron devant le Témoignage, pour être gardé comme signe pour les fils de la rébellion, afin que tu fasses cesser leurs murmures de dessus {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et qu’ils ne meurent pas. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Remets le bâton d’Aaron à sa place devant le Témoignage. Il doit y être gardé comme un signe pour les rebelles, afin que tu mettes fin à leurs plaintes contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et qu’ils ne meurent pas. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Remets le bâton d’Aaron devant l’arche. Garde-le là comme signe d’avertissement pour ceux qui se révoltent. Cela mettra fin à leurs plaintes contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ils ne mourront pas. »

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Irudishe fimbo ya Haruni mbele ya Ushuhuda, ihifadhiwe kuwa ishara kwa wana wa uasi, ili uyakomeshe manung'uniko yao kutoka juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao wasife."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Irudishe fimbo ya Haruni mahali pake mbele ya Ushuhuda. Itunzwe huko kuwa ishara kwa waasi, ili uyakomeshe malalamiko yao dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao wasife."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Irudishe fimbo ya Haruni mbele ya sanduku la agano. Itunze hapo kuwa ishara ya onyo kwa wale wanaoasi. Hii itakomesha malalamiko yao dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao hawatakufa."

decisions.choice: sons of rebellion: rebellious people
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a quality is a Hebrew way of describing people by it. The rebels are any in Israel who might rise up against God's choice again, as Korah and the congregation had done (16:1-3; 17:6).

decisions.choice: before the testimony, to be kept: the staff kept in the most holy place
decisions.reason: Like the jar of manna (Exodus 16:33-34), the staff was kept before the testimony as a lasting witness. Hebrews 9:4 speaks of it with the ark; 1 Kings 8:9 says that in Solomon's time only the stone tablets were inside the ark.

decisions.choice: so that they do not die: the sign is given to protect the people
decisions.reason: The grumbling had brought death twice in two days (16:35; 17:14). The sign is meant to settle the question so that no more of the people die for rebelling against God's choice.

decisions.choice: the rebels / those who rebel
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of "sons of rebellion"; Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: the ark
decisions.reason: Readable says "the ark" for "the testimony", the chest that held the covenant tablets (verse 19).

source.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹת֖וֹ כֵּ֥ן עָשָֽׂה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And did Moses; as commanded Yahweh him, so he did.

en.L: And Moses did [so]; just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him, so he did.
en.B: Moses did this. He did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.
en.R: Moses did exactly what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him.

es.L: Y Moisés [lo] hizo; tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado, así hizo.
es.B: Moisés lo hizo. Hizo tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado.
es.R: Moisés hizo exactamente lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado.

fr.L: Et Moïse fit [ainsi] ; comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui avait ordonné, ainsi il fit.
fr.B: Moïse fit ainsi. Il fit exactement comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le lui avait ordonné.
fr.R: Moïse a fait exactement ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait ordonné.

sw.L: Naye Musa akafanya [hivyo]; kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru, ndivyo alivyofanya.
sw.B: Musa alifanya hivyo. Alifanya sawasawa na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru.
sw.R: Musa alifanya kila kitu kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyomwamuru.

decisions.choice: he did ... so he did: Moses obeyed exactly
decisions.reason: The doubled "did" stresses that Moses carried out the command in full, as Exodus 40:16 says of the building of the tabernacle.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵ֥ן גָּוַ֛עְנוּ אָבַ֖דְנוּ כֻּלָּ֥נוּ אָבָֽדְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] sons of Israel to Moses, saying, look, we die, we perish, all of us, we perish.

en.L: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel said to Moses, saying, "Look, we are dying, we are perishing, all of us are perishing!
en.B: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} said to Moses, "We are dying! We are perishing, every one of us perishing!
en.R: Then the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} said to Moses, "We are going to die! We will all be destroyed!

es.L: Y los hijos de Israel hablaron a Moisés, diciendo: «¡He aquí, morimos, perecemos, todos nosotros perecemos!
es.B: Entonces los israelitas dijeron a Moisés: «¡Nos morimos! ¡Perecemos, perecemos todos!
es.R: Entonces los israelitas le dijeron a Moisés: «¡Vamos a morir! ¡Todos vamos a ser destruidos!

fr.L: Et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël parlèrent à Moïse, disant : « Voici, nous expirons, nous périssons, nous périssons tous !
fr.B: Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} dirent à Moïse : « Nous mourons ! Nous périssons, nous périssons tous jusqu’au dernier !
fr.R: Alors les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont dit à Moïse : « Nous allons mourir ! Nous allons tous être anéantis !

sw.L: Nao wana wa Israeli wakamwambia Musa, wakisema, "Tazama, tunakufa, tunaangamia, sisi sote tunaangamia!
sw.B: Kisha Waisraeli wakamwambia Musa, "Tunakufa! Tunaangamia, kila mmoja wetu anaangamia!
sw.R: Kisha Waisraeli wakamwambia Musa, "Tutakufa! Sote tutaangamizwa!

decisions.choice: we die, we perish: spoken as already happening
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form that presents an event as done. In a cry of fear it means that their death is certain and already upon them.

decisions.choice: perish: be lost, be destroyed
decisions.reason: The verb means to be lost or to come to ruin. Repeating it, with "all of us" between, shows the people's terror after the deaths of 16:31-35 and 17:14.

decisions.choice: the people's cry: from complaint to fear
decisions.reason: The day before they had blamed Moses and Aaron (verse 6). Now, having seen the sign, they fear that anyone who comes near the LORD's dwelling will die. Chapter 18 answers their fear: the priests and Levites will guard the sanctuary so that wrath does not fall on Israel again (18:1-7, 22-23).

decisions.choice: We are going to die
decisions.reason: Readable expresses the certainty of the Hebrew verb forms with "going to"; Literal and Balanced keep "we are dying".

source.text: כֹּ֣ל הַקָּרֵ֧ב׀הַקָּרֵ֛ב אֶל־מִשְׁכַּ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה יָמ֑וּת הַאִ֥ם תַּ֖מְנוּ לִגְוֺֽעַ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Every one coming near, the [one] coming near to [the] tabernacle of Yahweh, will die. Have we finished to perish?

en.L: Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, will die. Are we finished perishing?"
en.B: Whoever comes near, anyone who comes near the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, dies. Will we all perish to the last one?"
en.R: Whoever goes near the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dies! Will we all die, until no one is left?"

es.L: Todo el que se acerca, el que se acerca al tabernáculo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, morirá. ¿Hemos acabado de perecer?».
es.B: Cualquiera que se acerca, cualquiera que se acerca al tabernáculo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, muere. ¿Vamos a perecer todos hasta el último?».
es.R: ¡El que se acerca al tabernáculo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} muere! ¿Vamos a morir todos, hasta que no quede nadie?».

fr.L: Quiconque s’approche, quiconque s’approche de la Demeure {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, mourra. Avons-nous fini de périr ? »
fr.B: Quiconque s’approche, quiconque s’approche de la Demeure {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, meurt. Allons-nous tous périr jusqu’au dernier ? »
fr.R: Celui qui s’approche de la Demeure {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} meurt ! Allons-nous tous mourir, jusqu’à ce qu’il ne reste plus personne ? »

decisions.choice: everyone who comes near, who comes near: anyone at all who comes close
decisions.reason: The word for one who comes near is repeated for emphasis: anyone at all who goes close to the tabernacle. The people had seen the 250 die for drawing near with incense (16:35; 17:5).

decisions.choice: are we finished perishing: will we all die until none of us is left
decisions.reason: The question uses a verb meaning to be complete or come to an end. It most likely asks whether the dying will go on until every one of them is dead. It could also be read as "Will our dying never end?" Both readings voice the same fear.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle of the LORD: the LORD's dwelling among them
decisions.reason: The tabernacle was the tent where the LORD lived among his people (Exodus 25:8-9). His holiness, so near, now fills the people with dread.
